[[File:Emt2016.png|thumb|Eugene Terentjev in 2016]]
'''Eugene M. Terentjev''' (born 21 June 1959) is professor of [[Polymer physics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], and fellow of [[Queens' College, Cambridge|Queens' College]] where he is the Director of Studies in Natural Sciences.

Terentjev earned his MSc in physics from [[Moscow State University]], and his PhD from Institute of Crystallography, [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], Moscow. He then carried out postdoctoral research at [[Case Western Reserve University]] in [[Cleveland, Ohio]], before moving to Cambridge in 1992. 
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/directory/terentjeve|title=Professor Eugene Terentjev — Department of Physics|website=Phy.cam.ac.uk|date=31 July 2013 |accessdate=11 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.queens.cam.ac.uk/professor-eugene-terentjev|title=Professor Eugene Terentjev - Queens' College|website=Queens.cam.ac.uk|accessdate=11 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/healthcare/article/cambridge-students-horrified-by-hard-work-claims-professor-eugene-terentjev-7t9f8jt6l|title=Cambridge students 'horrified' by hard work claims Professor Eugene Terentjev|author=Rosemary Bennett|date=8 November 2017|access-date=11 November 2017|newspaper=[[The Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/2017/11/07/cambridge-professor-warned-against-partying-accused-students/|title=Cambridge professor who warned against partying is accused by students of risking mental health damage|first=Camilla|last=Turner|date=7 November 2017|accessdate=11 November 2017|newspaper=The Telegraph}}</ref> Terentjev's [[h-index]] is over 83, with over 26000 citations to his articles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=5DOZG-oAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Eugene Terentjev - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2020-04-24}}</ref> His most notable contributions are in the scientific field of liquid crystal elastomers,<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-MwTDAAAQBAJ|title=Liquid Crystal Elastomers|date=9 October 2003 |publisher=OUP Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-852767-1 |access-date=2020-04-24}}</ref> and in biophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2021-08-mathematical-muscle.html|title=Mathematical model predicts best way to build muscle|website=phys.org/news|access-date=2021-08-24}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* "Liquid crystal elastomers: 30 years after"  E.M. Terentjev:  ''Macromolecules'', 58, 2792-2806 (2025).
* "Mechanism of pressure-sensitive adhesion in nematic elastomers" H. Guo, M.O. Saed, E.M. Terentjev: ''Macromolecules'' 56, 6247-6255 (2023).
* "F1 rotary motor of ATP synthase is driven by the torsionally asymmetric drive shaft."  O. Kulish, A.D. Wright, E.M. Terentjev:  ''Sci. Rep.'', 6, 28180 (2016).
* "How cells feel: stochastic model for a molecular mechanosensor."  M. Escude, M.K. Rigozzi, E.M. Terentjev:  ''Biophys. J.'', 106, 124–133 (2014).
* "Mouldable liquid-crystalline elastomer actuators with exchangeable covalent bonds."  Z. Pei, Y. Yang, Q. Chen, E.M. Terentjev, Y.Wei, Y. Ji: ''Nature Mater.'' 13,  36-41 (2013).
* "A chain mechanism for flagellum growth."  L.D.B. Evans, S. Poulter, E.M. Terentjev, C. Hughes, G.M. Fraser: ''Nature'', 504, 287-290 (2013).
* "Strength of nanotubes, filaments and nanowires from sonication-induced scission."  Y.Y. Huang, T.P.J. Knowles and E.M. Terentjev: ''Adv. Mater.'' 21, 1–4  (2009).
* "Photo-mechanical actuation in polymer-nanotube composites."  S.V. Ahir, E.M. Terentjev: ''Nature Mater.'' 4, 491–495 (2005).
